svg.title: Sality P2P botnet kill chain - infection, peer mesh, signed tasking, EggJagger and the 2026-08-31 sinkhole
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, the infected endpoint: 1 infection by executable infection, removable media and shares, 2 stealth and persistence through a polymorphic stub, injection and a security-killing driver (2011 detail), 3 membership of the peer-to-peer mesh with a 40 minute peer check, 4 receipt of an RSA-signed URL pack and HTTP payload download, 5 the EggJagger clipboard hijacker replacing wallet addresses, 6 other payloads including credential theft, spam, proxy and DDoS, 7 the 2026-08-31 disruption that cuts the bot off from its operator while the malware stays installed. Right lane, the operation: A the SALTY SPIDER operator since 2003, B two P2P networks v3 and v4 with separate keys, C super peers and the reputation based peer list, D URL pack hosts, E the payload economy, F the CrowdStrike and law enforcement disruption with the lighthouse sinkhole 188.166.101.148. Critical stages are shown in red.
svg.text: Sality: P2P botnet poisoned through its own peer list
Vendor: CrowdStrike + DOJ - Date: 2026-09-01 - Cluster: SALTY SPIDER (Sality) - Day 111
INFECTED ENDPOINT (what defenders see)
SALITY OPERATION (P2P network)
Infection of an endpoint
Infected executables, removable drives and network shares
carry the file infector; a user runs an infected program
Started in 2003 as a file-infecting virus
T1091 Removable Media T1204.002 User Execution
legacy: autorun.inf + random-name copy
Stealth and persistence (2011 detail)
Polymorphic entry-point stub in .exe and .scr files,
injection into processes, kernel driver kills security tools
2026 report does not republish these; treat as legacy leads
service amsint32 SafeBoot keys deleted
Joins the peer-to-peer mesh
Keeps a list of super peers; checks liveness every 40 min
Reputation rises with answers, silent peers are purged
No peer authentication, no allowlist, no C2 server
T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol
hunt: UDP fan-out in 40-minute cycles
Receives a signed URL pack and downloads payloads
Hard-coded RSA public keys verify URL and file packs
Payloads fetched over HTTP from compromised or free sites
Defenders as peers cannot push code of their own
T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer T1071.001
v3 pack 25202, v4 pack 31010
EggJagger clipboard hijacker swaps wallet addresses
Main payload for about eight years: watches the clipboard
for crypto wallet addresses and substitutes the operator's
At least 12.1M roubles (about 150k USD) stolen per vendor
T1565.002 Transmitted Data Manipulation
test: clipboard canary on finance hosts
Other payloads: credentials, spam, proxy, DDoS
Credential theft, spam relay, proxy service, exploitation
DDoS: forex2030.com 2016, kharkovforum.com 2022-02-25,
AvanChange exchange 2023 (payload compiled seconds before)
T1498 Network Denial of Service
over 33,000 infected machines per CrowdStrike
Disruption 2026-08-31: bot cut off, malware stays
Peer lists poisoned; bots contact the sinkhole and are purged
Operator sees infected machines simply disappear
Malware remains active on victims and must be removed
UDP to 188.166.101.148 = infected host
do not block the lighthouse; Shadowserver notifies
A
Operator SALTY SPIDER (CrowdStrike name)
Running Sality since 2003; one operator behind v3 and v4
No country, individual or charge announced
Clipboard theft, spam and DDoS payloads pushed over the years
confidence: high (infra), none (identity)
CrowdStrike CAO 2026-09-01, DOJ 26-149
B
Two P2P networks: v3 and v4
Shared codebase, incompatible protocols, different keys
v3 embeds a 128-byte RSA key, v4 a 256-byte key
YARA: IPFILTERDRIVER string plus the key bytes
v3 key starts 99 65 40 34 cd ae 9d b3
v4 key starts bb d2 96 8e ed 0b 93 8a
C
Super peers and the peer list
Publicly reachable infected hosts form the backbone
Peer list is the one structure every bot trusts
Most bots sit behind NAT and call out during maintenance
attack surface chosen by the disruption
liveness check every 40 minutes
D
URL pack payload hosts
v3 pack 25202: 7 compromised or free-hosted sites
v4 pack 31010: gatheredovertime.com and imagebucket.biz
Host alone is weak; host plus path is the indicator
gatheredovertime.com/nb4 imagebucket.biz/nv4
theunforgiven.p8.hu/img/top.gif and 6 more
E
Payload economy
EggJagger clipboard hijacker is the main earner
Spam, credential theft, proxy and exploitation payloads
Three documented DDoS campaigns 2016 to 2023
no hashes or wallet addresses published
unspent portfolio peaked near 147M roubles 2025-01
F
Disruption by CrowdStrike and law enforcement
Peer-list poisoning, sinkholes, payload URLs taken down
DOJ, FBI, DCIS, Shadowserver; Europol, Eurojust; BG HU RO
Precedents: GameOver Zeus 2014, Kelihos 2017
lighthouse sinkhole 188.166.101.148 (UDP)
executed Monday 2026-08-31, announced 2026-09-01
Detection anchors: UDP to 188.166.101.148, last URL packs, embedded RSA key prefixes, legacy host artifacts, UDP fan-out
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-04, KQL k1-k3, YARA sality_p2p_botnet.yar, Suricata sids 6280001-6280006, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
The takedown cuts tasking but removes nothing: file infectors live inside legitimate files, so recovery is rebuild from clean media.
No hashes or domains were published; legacy rows from the 2011 Symantec analysis are low confidence for 2026 builds.
